page: Microsoft Azure D8a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7763 processor configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores, supporting simultaneous multithreading at 2 threads per core. The dedicated CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz and features 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. Memory capacity is 32.0 GB, yielding a standard general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage includes 215 GB of local SSD capacity, while GPU accelerators are absent.

Benchmark results position the D8a_v4 predominantly in the middle tier of performance. Geekbench testing yields a single-core score of 1561.0 and a multi-core score of 6259.0, reflecting average throughput across tasks such as Clang software compilation (7322.0), ray tracing (9191.0), and image processing (6600.0). PassMark evaluations align with this profile, posting an overall CPU score of 11954.75, an encryption score of 8675.85, and a database operations score of 3594.1. Cached read memory bandwidth reaches 514.53 GB/sec, while uncached large-block reads reach 42.8 GB/sec.

Tradeoffs appear primarily under sustained synthetic CPU stress and memory write-heavy workloads. The instance registers poor single-core stress-ng performance (770.98, bottom 10%) and weak multi-core stress-ng performance (3078.76, bottom 25%). Furthermore, large-block memory write bandwidth is limited to 24.77 GB/sec, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 33.01 GB/sec, placing both in the bottom 25%. Advanced vector extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX are not supported, though standard AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions are available.

The 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio paired with balanced average scores in Redis SET throughput (8.06 million operations/sec) and static web serving (9.56 GB/sec) makes the D8a_v4 cost-effective for standard enterprise compute needs. It is suitable for medium-load web servers, application backends, mid-sized relational databases, caching layers, and software development pipelines that do not require specialized high-density vector instructions or sustained floating-point compute saturation.
description: Microsoft Azure D8a_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with an 8-vCPU AMD EPYC 7763 processor (4 physical cores at 3.525 GHz), 32.0 GB of RAM, and 215 GB of local SSD storage. Designed with a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, it delivers mid-tier performance across varied benchmarks, including Geekbench multi-core (6259.0), Redis operations (8.06 million ops/sec), and static web serving (9.56 GB/sec). The architecture supports AES, VAES, and SHA-NI cryptographic instructions, although it lacks AVX-512 extensions and exhibits lower scores in sustained stress-ng tests and large-block memory writes. With dedicated CPU allocation and local SSD storage, the D8a_v4 provides a balanced hardware footprint well suited for enterprise application hosting, relational databases, caching clusters, and standard build or CI/CD pipelines.
